transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?
I came in because I’m so tired I can barely get through a shift. It feels like my body’s full of wet sand, and even resting doesn’t really bring me back.
Have you noticed, or has anyone told you, that you snore loudly or seem to stop breathing for moments while you're asleep?
I’m not really sure. Nobody’s told me that I snore or stop breathing, and I wouldn’t notice it myself.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, or been feeling persistently down or sad?
Yeah. Things I normally like—cooking, playing guitar, hiking, even going to see my family—just feel flat. I do them sometimes, but it feels like I’m pretending to care.
How long have you been feeling this low interest and flat mood - has it been going on for a couple of weeks, or longer, like months?
It’s been longer than a couple weeks—about four months, I think. The low, empty feeling stayed after that first burst of energy at work wore off.
Over the past four months, have you noticed any unintentional weight gain or weight loss?
I think I’ve lost some weight. My appetite’s been all over the place, but lately I mostly forget to eat, or food just tastes like cardboard. My work pants have been fitting looser.
Have you noticed feeling unusually cold, or needing more layers than usual, compared to other people around you?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed needing extra layers more than anyone else.
Have you ever had a period like this before—weeks or months of low mood and losing interest in things—at any other point in your life, prior to these last four months?
I’m not sure. I can’t really think of another time it lasted like this.
Have you noticed feeling unusually short of breath or your heart racing with everyday activities, or has anyone commented that you look pale?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed anything like that, and no one’s said I look pale.
Have you noticed yourself sleeping much longer than usual at night or needing frequent naps during the day, even when you have the chance to rest?
No, not really. With my shifts changing, I got to where I’d only sleep a few hours and still feel wired. Now even when I’m exhausted, I wake up early and my mind is already going.
